title: Insalata di Rinforzo
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A tangy Neapolitan Christmas cauliflower salad tossed with olives, capers, anchovies, and pickled vegetables, its name meaning 'reinforcement' since it's kept on the table to be replenished throughout the holidays.
longDesc: Insalata di rinforzo is designed to be practical as much as delicious, its vinegar-based dressing allowing it to keep well over several days, ready to be 'reinforced' with fresh cauliflower and toppings as the Neapolitan holiday season stretches on.
ingredients: 80 g (½ cup) mixed pickled vegetables (giardiniera), chopped
100 ml (scant ½ cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the cauliflower florets until just tender, about 6–8 minutes; do not overcook, as they should retain some bite.
Combine the cauliflower with the olives, capers, anchovies, and pickled vegetables in a large bowl.
Whisk together the vinegar and olive oil, season, and pour over the salad.
Toss well and let sit for at least a few hours, ideally overnight, before serving to let the flavors meld.
Toss again before serving and adjust seasoning to taste.
chefTips: Don't overcook the cauliflower — it should retain a slight bite rather than becoming soft and mushy.
This salad genuinely improves with time, so making it a day ahead is traditional and recommended.
The vinegar-forward dressing is what allows this dish to keep well over the extended Neapolitan holiday period.
commonMistakes: Overcooking the cauliflower, resulting in a mushy rather than pleasantly firm texture.
Serving immediately without letting the flavors rest and develop.
Being too sparing with the vinegar, which is essential both for flavor and for how well the dish keeps.
servedWith: As part of a Neapolitan Christmas antipasto spread
storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days; flavor improves over the first couple of days.
reheating: Not applicable; served cold or at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Cauliflower provides fiber and vitamin C.
culturalNote: Insalata di rinforzo is a fixture of the Neapolitan Christmas table, its practical, long-keeping nature reflected directly in its name, meaning 'reinforcement salad.'
